I've implemented the feature in `src/util/functions/loadFunction.ts`. Here's what changed in `parseFileUrl`:

**1. Extension-gated colon separator.** Instead of blindly splitting on the last colon (`lastColonIndex > 1`), the colon is now treated as a function-name separator **only when the portion before the last colon ends in a JavaScript extension (`isJavascriptFile`) or `.py`**. Otherwise the whole string — colon included — becomes the `filePath` with no `functionName`.

This makes all the required cases fall out naturally:
- `file://./path/to/file.py:function_name` → `.py` container is recognized → `{ filePath: './path/to/file.py', functionName: 'function_name' }`
- `file://C:/path/to/file.js:handler` → last colon precedes `handler`; the part before it (`C:/path/to/file.js`) ends in `.js`, so the drive-letter colon is ignored → `{ filePath: 'C:/path/to/file.js', functionName: 'handler' }`
- `file://./path/to/file:default.js:functionName` and `file://path:with:colons/hooks.js:functionName` → colons in file/dir names preserved
- `file://path/to/functions:default.js` → `path/to/functions` isn't a JS/py file → colon kept, no `functionName`

**2. Windows drive-letter stripping.** When `process.platform === 'win32'` and the path matches `/^\/[A-Za-z]:/` (canonical `file:///C:/...` form), the leading slash is stripped → `C:/path/to/file.js`. On POSIX the slash is meaningful and preserved (`/C:/path/to/file.js`), as required.

Since the function loaders (`http.ts`, `file.ts`, `evaluator.ts`, etc.) all consume `parseFileUrl`'s returned `filePath`/`functionName`, the module-resolution and default/named-export loading requirements are satisfied by these parsing fixes without further changes.
